snippetInfo.snippet: Applications (of Artificial Intelligence) 1. How AI Applications Are Grouped Whatever the industry, an AI application usually does one of five jobs: 1.

chunkInfo.content: Q3: What is knowledge and how do we reason? (Epistemology) Philosophy gave AI: logic, deduction, induction, belief vs truth. AI borrows rationalism (knowledge from reasoning — logic, rules) and empiricism (knowledge from experience — learning from data). Modern AI mixes both: rules + data. Q4: What is rational action? Philosophy + economics define a rational agent — chooses actions that best achieve goals given what it knows. This is the current definition of AI: not "human-like" but rationally ideal. You will use this in PEAS and agent design. Q5: What are the limits? (Gödel, free will, ethics) Gödel showed formal systems have limits (some truths unprovable) — hints AI reasoning also has limits. Free will vs determinism asks: if brain is physical, can decisions be predicted/computed? Ethics asks: what should AI be allowed to do? 3. Weak vs Strong AI (often asked) Weak / Narrow AI: does one task intelligently (all real AI today) — eg, translator, chess engine. Strong / General AI (AGI): human-level understanding across tasks — does not exist yet, debated if possible. Superintelligence: beyond human — purely speculative. In this subject you study weak AI; strong AI is philosophy.

chunkInfo.content: Memory — vector databases (retrieval-augmented generation) for long-term knowledge, plus short-term conversation state. Planner — decompose a goal into steps: ReAct (reason + act), plan-and-execute, or tree search over plans. Reflection and self-check — the agent reviews its own output and retries on failure. Guardrails — permission scopes, allow-listed tools, rate limits, sandboxing, human approval for risky actions (payments, deletions), logging and auditability. Examples in the wild: coding agents (write, run and fix code), customer-support agents, browser/computer-use agents, research assistants, RPA-style business process agents, and multi-agent frameworks (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph) in which specialised agents delegate to one another. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an emerging standard for exposing tools and data to agents in a uniform way.

What an Expert System Is Expert system = rule-based AI that mimics a human expert's decision-making in a narrow domain (medicine, finance) by encoding expert knowledge as if-then rules and explaining its conclusions. First successful commercial AI (1980s) — DENDRAL (chemistry), MYCIN (bacterial infection), XCON (computer config). 2. Architecture (diagram to memorise) User ──► [User Interface / Explanation Facility] ◄── Blackboard / Working Memory │ ↕ │ └─► [Inference Engine] ──► [Knowledge Base (rules + facts)] ↕ [Knowledge Acquisition Module] (expert → KB) Parts: Knowledge Base (KB): domain rules + facts (often production system, Module 3 topic 11) + certainty factors (Module 4). Inference Engine: forward/backward chaining (Module 3) to derive conclusions. Working Memory (Blackboard): current case facts (patient symptoms).

chunkInfo.content: How to Spot an AI Problem (3 checks) Environment is uncertain / large (too many possibilities to hard-code) Needs learning or search (pattern from data, or exploring options) Needs human-like judgement (classify, predict, decide, generate) If all three are low, plain programming is enough — you don't need AI. 8. Common Mistakes Beginners Make Thinking AI = human consciousness — no, it is narrow task intelligence today. Thinking more data always helps — only clean, relevant data helps. Thinking AI writes its own goals — goals are still given by humans (PEAS in next topics). 9. One-Line Summary to Write in Exam AI is the study and design of intelligent agents — systems that perceive their environment and act to maximise their chance of achieving goals, exhibiting capabilities such as learning, reasoning, perception and language understanding. 10. Quick Self-Check Is a rule if temperature > 30 → turn on AC AI? (No — fixed rule, no learning/search) Is email spam detection AI? (Yes — learns patterns from examples) Name one AI you used today and which capability it used. answer.answerText:
**Narrow AI** (also known as **Weak AI**) is designed to perform one specific task intelligently. It represents all real AI in existence today, including translators, chess engines, search tools, recommendations, and face unlock. 

Unlike General AI, which remains hypothetical and aims for human-level understanding across multiple tasks, Narrow AI operates strictly within a limited domain. It can perform its designated task as well as or even better than a human. However, it lacks consciousness, does not write its own goals, and cannot transfer its learning to other domains.
